label: late-episode GO ramp, steeper after a2 choice and after no reward
terms: (phase == GO) * (ep_trial >= 90) * (ep_trial - 90) ;; (phase == GO) * (ep_trial >= 90) * (prev_reward == 0) ;; (phase == GO) * (ep_trial >= 90) * np.clip(-belief_lo, -4, 4) ;; (phase == GO) * (ep_trial >= 90) * (prev_action == 2) ;; (phase == GO) * (ep_trial >= 90) * (prev_reward == 0) * (prev_action == 2) ;; (phase == GO) * (ep_trial >= 90) * (tv("reward", -2) == 0) ;; (phase == GO) * (ep_trial >= 90) * (prev_reward == 0) * (ep_trial - 90) ;; (phase == GO) * (ep_trial >= 90) * (prev_action == 2) * (ep_trial - 90)
explanation: Fires essentially only at GO in the last ~10 trials of the episode (timing alone R^2 0.42). Within trials 90-99 its magnitude is a ramp in ep_trial whose slope depends on the previous trial: steep (~+0.38/trial) after an a2 choice, a further ~+0.23/trial after an unrewarded trial, and nearly flat after a rewarded a1 trial; so it acts like a rectified ramp whose onset is earlier after a2 and no reward. A belief term (ideal-observer log-odds toward S2 good, i.e. evidence for a2) adds positively, as does an unrewarded trial two back. D1 and D2 carry nothing. The fit is multiplicative (ramp x condition); the additive per-phase tables in the profile score only 0.03 (the all ceiling), because they miss the interaction with the late-episode ramp. Observed-only terms, no model outputs: test R^2 beyond timing 0.59 (dev 0.65). The earlier value/policy-based label (low-value signal, choosing a2) is matched here by prev_action == 2, prev_reward == 0 and belief_lo, so the observed-only version gives up little; I did not score a direct comparison against model value/policy.

issues: The 8 terms really contain only 7 independent directions. Adding tv('reward',-2)==0 on top of the six prev_action/prev_reward ramp terms plus belief gives exactly the same test R^2 (0.5867) as the original set, so that term adds nothing a reparameterisation doesn't. Swapping it for a quadratic ramp (ep_trial-90)**2 lifts test R^2 to 0.611, over the 0.6 bar, so the ramp is slightly convex rather than linear.

The 'explained' verdict leans on the 80%-of-ceiling rule against an additive 'all' ceiling of 0.03. That ceiling cannot capture the ramp x condition interaction, so it means nothing here. The verdict therefore really rests on 0.59, which is just under 0.6. The 0.611 alternative above clears the bar, so the verdict survives.

'Starts at zero and switches on earlier after a2' is loose. The fitted offsets are large and negative (prev_action==2: -1.89, prev_reward==0: -0.78) alongside the steeper slopes (+0.38, +0.23 per trial). After a2 the prediction is lower than after a1 in trials 90-94 and only overtakes it later. That is a steeper ramp crossing over, not an earlier onset.

Checked components each carry a real share. Test R^2 is 0.39 for the prev_action ramp alone, 0.28 for the prev_reward ramp, 0.22 for the belief ramp, and 0.52 for the prev-trial terms combined. Dropping belief (keeping the quadratic ramp) gives 0.554 against 0.611. Using the future current choice (action==2) instead of prev_action does no better (0.40 against 0.39), so the observed-only choice proxy loses nothing.

No large systematic error class remains. Mean errors by phase are under 0.01 and the largest phase x previous-trial biases are GO after a1 S2 r (-0.06) and GO after a2 S2 r... more precisely GO after a2 S1 r (+0.04), both small against a feature std of 0.36. The leftover variance shows up as on/off variability within late a2 streaks: actual 5-6 against predicted 2.5, or actual 0 against predicted 3. No prev-trial or belief term tracks it.
'D1 and D2 carry nothing' is slightly overstated. D2 activations up to about 1 appear late in the episode (examples show D2 values of 0.3-0.99). They are small and rare.
